utility.value: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP)
utility.notes: LADWP's own official site describes itself as the largest municipally-owned utility in the United States, providing electric and water service to the City of Los Angeles.

value.name: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP)
value.notes: LADWP is a vertically-integrated municipal utility (like Pasadena Water and Power) — it generates and delivers its own power rather than sitting alongside a separate CCA. No Community Choice Aggregator was found serving the City of Los Angeles in the sources reviewed this session.

permit_authority.value: Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety (LADBS)
permit_authority.notes: LADBS, not LADWP, issues the building permit for solar installations — LADWP's role is limited to the separate net-metering interconnection process (see interconnection_url). Both ladbs.org and dbs.lacity.gov returned HTTP 403 to direct automated fetch this session; confirmed via consistent, independent search-engine indexing of official LADBS publications (its own Express Permit information bulletin and Eligibility Checklist for Expedited Solar Photovoltaic Installations).

permit_url.notes: Same LADBS direct-fetch limitation as permit_authority.

interconnection_url.notes: ladwp.com returned HTTP 403 to direct automated fetch; confirmed via consistent search-engine indexing describing LADWP's NEM interconnection application process (obtaining an Interconnection Work Request Number via ladwp.com/nem).

value.name: Self-Generation Incentive Program (SGIP) — Residential Solar and Storage Equity (RSSE)
value.administrator: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP)
value.description: Contrary to the assumption in an earlier pass of this record, LADWP is a genuine SGIP Program Administrator for the state-funded (AB 209) Residential Solar and Storage Equity budget — confirmed directly on LADWP's own SGIP page, which describes SGIP as providing funding for income-qualified residential customers to install solar and battery storage. Eligibility is income- and housing-type-restricted, not general-market: single-family households must document total household income at or below 80% of Area Median Income (AMI); multifamily properties must have 5+ deed-restricted low-income rental units and meet an additional disadvantaged-community or low-income-household threshold. No specific dollar incentive rate is stated on LADWP's own page; current step-based rates are tracked separately by the statewide SGIP administrator at selfgenca.com.
value.eligibility: LADWP residential customers meeting SGIP RSSE's income/housing criteria (single-family: household income at or below 80% AMI with tax documentation; multifamily: 5+ deed-restricted low-income units meeting an additional disadvantaged-community or low-income-household threshold). Not available to general-market (non-income-qualified) customers.

value.required_when: systems 10 kW or less in a one- or two-family dwelling, meeting the Express Permit checklist

value.required_when: always, for grid interconnection/net energy metering

required_documents.notes: Both LADBS's Express Permit application and LADWP's separate interconnection application are described consistently across independent search results, though neither official page could be directly fetched this session (both 403 blocked).

inspection_steps.notes: Not confirmed this session — LADBS's own inspection-request page (ladbs.org) could not be directly fetched.

value.notes: LADBS's own Express Permit process is described as requiring no plan check for eligible systems, issued online — consistent with a fast/expedited process, but no source found stated a specific same-day or numeric business-day timeline for either the LADBS permit or the LADWP interconnection/NEM approval step, so no day range is recorded.

value.program_or_pathway: LADBS Express Permit (no plan check required)
other_conditions: LADWP's own NEM program offers a 'Fast Track Process' for systems under 10 kW, skipping the performance meter test
No individual LADWP customer can apply for net metering with a system larger than 1 megawatt (MW)
Express Permits are issued online only via dbs.lacity.gov

eligibility_constraints.notes: The 10 kW figure is consistently stated for LADBS's Express Permit eligibility across independent sources; the unit (AC vs DC) was not explicitly specified, recorded here as AC per the more common convention for this size class.

permit_fees.notes: Not stated in the sources reviewed this session.

rebates.notes: LADWP's 'Solar Rooftops Program' referenced in some sources appears to be a separate leased/shared-solar program (mentioning lease payments to participants), distinct from a standard rebate for a customer-owned system — not recorded here as a rebate since its structure was not independently confirmed as a rebate in this session.

official_contacts.notes: Contact details found via consistent search-engine indexing; not independently fetched this session (both domains 403 blocked).
